style: set the scene in one or two plain sentences

candidates.angle: केवलैः, the word for merely, showing that action is done without attachment to the instruments
tyaktva, giving up attachment, which is the key action
yoginah, the one who acts, and atmaśuddhaye, for inner purification, showing the aim of action
candidates.evidence: योगिनः कर्म कुर्वन्ति ... आत्मशुद्धये (Yogis perform action ... for inner purification)

angle_en: tyaktva: the act of giving up attachment
angle_hi: tyaktva: आसक्ति का त्याग करने का काम

en.intro: Picture a practitioner who keeps working but stays untouched by the outcome. This verse lists every part of a person that acts, and the one thing that is left behind.
en.notice: The word tyaktva means having given up, and it is the turning point of the verse. The yogi performs action with body, mind, intellect, and senses, yet the one thing dropped is attachment.
en.next: Krishna then explains what happens when this letting go is done, and what happens when it is not.
en.meaning: Yogis perform action with body, mind, intellect, and the senses, giving up attachment, only for inner purification.

hi.intro: एक ऐसे योगी की कल्पना कीजिए जो काम करता रहता है लेकिन नतीजों से अछूता रहता है। यह श्लोक इंसान के हर उस अंग की सूची देता है जिससे काम होता है, और उस एक चीज़ की जो पीछे छूट जाती है।
hi.meaning: कर्मयोगी शरीर, मन, बुद्धि और इन्द्रियों द्वारा कर्म करते हैं और ममतारहित होकर केवल अन्तःकरण की शुद्धिके लिए ही कर्म करते हैं।
hi.next: कृष्ण आगे बताते हैं कि जब यह त्याग किया जाता है तो क्या मिलता है, और जब नहीं किया जाता तो क्या होता है।

issues: meaning_changed: "यहाँ शब्द tyaktva का मतलब है त्यागना" (The source explicitly defines tyaktva as 'tyāgtvā' (having given up). The script says 'tyāktvā' means 'tyāgnā' (abandoning/renouncing), which is a different grammatical form and meaning.)

borrowed: "The word tyāgtvā means having given up, and it is the turning point of the verse." (The English intro explicitly states that the verse lists 'every part of a person that acts, and the one thing that is left behind.' The English notice then explicitly names that one thing as 'attachment,' which is the core message of verse 10 (the lotus leaf untouched by water), not verse 11. The Hindi notice repeats this borrowed content by saying 'जो एक चीज़ पीछे छोड़ देते हैं वह है आसक्ति' (the one thing left behind is attachment). This presents the thematic content of the previous verse as if it belongs to this verse.)
